analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. The one changed range is head line 397, which adds a table row documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL. The row says exact `0` disables the control, the default is on, and it is read once per process and not forwarded to LaunchAgents. It describes a library attention-path optimization in libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../AttentionV1.swift: full-attention prompt chunks use one fused causal SDPA call on either KV backend, excluding live packed paged KV.

The supplied evidence is documentation only, so there is no code change in the provider or coordinator, and no change to trust boundaries, keys, attestation, the App Attest authorization path or the prefix-cache storage or crypto path. I found no new authorization, data-exposure or billing surface in the docs. The row claims no security guarantee and no change to coordinator policy.

The changed row at head line 397 sits inside the 'Provider CLI' table. That table is not part of the supplied head text, which shows only 1–353 of the file. Base text 519–686 is unchanged context: it covers the diffusion, Bonsai, prefix-cache, hashing and GPT-OSS controls, none of which this PR edits.

Remaining question: the underlying source change is not supplied, so the kernel path, causal masking correctness and any effect on cross-request isolation (T-028, T-041) are unverified. Fused SDPA could in principle affect numerical output or the KV-cache timing side channel (SEC-035 accepted risk). The documented env var is a process-local performance switch with a rollback, and nothing here shows an isolation regression. Reviewers of the code PR, if there is one, should check that the fused causal mask is correct for chunked prefill with a prefix-cache-restored offset, since a wrong mask could leak future-token information within a request only, not across tenants. The head text for the changed range is also truncated in this batch.
